newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Brent steady, NYMEX down, weekend squaring seen.
newsitem.headline: Brent steady, NYMEX down, weekend squaring seen.

text.p: September Brent crude futures were untraded but steady on Friday, although NYMEX gave up some overnight gains in modest ACCESS trading.
September Brent crude on SIMEX was quoted at midday at $18.34/$18.47 per barrel, after the contract in London rose five cents to settle at $18.44.
NYMEX September futures rose 14 cents in New York, helped again by a firm gasoline market, where the August contract added 1.09 cent to 62.21.
But the spectre of a flood of Iraq crude export to meet a September deadline for sales worth $1 billion was hanging over world crude markets.
Brokers said the spectre might tempt some squaring of positions Friday to limit exposure to any weekend announcements.
Members of the United Nations sanctions committee said on Thursday that Baghdad would not receive permission to extend its deadline for the first tranche of sales.
Currently, Iraq has six weeks in which to sell the first $1 billion worth, raising the prospect of a flood of crude hitting the market.
